BiblicalUsage: Adoram — the same man as Adoniram — was over the tribute under David, Solomon, and Rehoboam. He is the one Rehoboam sent to the rebellious tribes after Solomon's death, hoping his old authority would calm them, and the people stoned him instead.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Adoram's end shows what happens when a king answers a people with force instead of listening. The man who had collected tribute for forty years became the first casualty of the split, and no title could protect him.
